title: Phylogenetic trait memory is lineage-contingent rather than trait-intrinsic across plant families
central_claim: Family context contributes a modest repeatable component to phylogenetic trait memory, but trait identity carries little robust information that transfers to an unseen family.

required_interpretation.portability: Little transferable trait-level signal; not anti-portability.
required_interpretation.family_context: Repeatable lineage context; biological mechanism unresolved.
required_interpretation.residual: Do not interpret the original 80.6% residual as biological system specificity.
required_interpretation.scale: All-201 natural-log sensitivity remains HOLD; no offset or selected-subset rescue.

stop_rule: No new SE estimator, trait transformation, redundancy grouping, family/trait filtering, portability predictor, or phylogenetic-signal metric may be selected on these outcomes to strengthen RC1.

technical_amendment.reason: Paper-package verifier previously treated the explicit nonclaim phrase 'trait identity is anti-portable' as if it were an affirmative manuscript claim. The verifier now checks for the preferred weak-portability interpretation and allows the phrase only in the explicit nonclaim section.
